 Order

Annexure-A12 order of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-I, Ottappalam, refusing to direct further investigation in Crime No.566/2021 of Ottappalam Police Station, is under challenge in this petition filed by the de facto complainant under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-I, Ottappalam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The final report filed in the said crime relating to the commission of offence under Section 498A I.P.C, was accepted to files as C.C No.515/2021 by the learned Magistrate.

The de facto complainant had earlier filed Crl.M.P No.3831/2021 before the learned Magistrate for further investigation stating the reason that the Investigating Officer did not conduct investigation in respect of several other allegations raised by the de facto complainant.
As per Annexure-A7 order dated 10.01.2022, the learned Magistrate allowed the above petition in part and directed the Investigating Officer to conduct a further investigation.

Accordingly, the Deputy Superintendent of Police, Shornur conducted further investigation and filed Annexure-A10 supplementary final report incorporating the offences under Sections 323, 324, 294(b) and 506(ii) I.P.C also, in addition to Section 498A I.P.C. Dissatisfied with the above 2025:KER:57265 Crl.M.C No.2377/2025    3        supplementary final report, the de facto complainant filed Crl.M.P No.3206/2023 before the learned Magistrate contending that the Investigating Officer had not included the offence under Section 308 I.P.C, nor recovered the weapons used by the accused for the commission of the crime,
and hence further investigation has to be again ordered.

The learned Magistrate, by the impugned order dated 11.12.2024, dismissed the above petition with the observation that there is no evidence prima facie to order a re-investigation (sic-appears to be a misnomer for further investigation) to include Section 308 I.P.C. It is the aforesaid order, which is under challenge in this petition.

2.
Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor representing the State of Kerala.
3. The alleged physical assault of the second respondent/accused upon the de facto complainant is the subject matter of this crime.

The de facto complainant, in her statement given to the Investigating Officer, had alleged that the second respondent had hit her upon her head with a curtain rod, grabbed her neck and brandished a knife with the threat that she would be eliminated.
The aforesaid acts are alleged to have been committed by the second respondent on 2025:KER:57265 Crl.M.C No.2377/2025    4        22.03.2021 and 24.03.2021, while they were residing at Chennai.
The 14 year old son of the petitioner and the second respondent is said to have witnessed the above physical assault of the second respondent upon the petitioner.

According to the petitioner, the statements given by her to the police, and her son to the Magistrate,
would clearly indicate that the act of the second respondent in the above regard would constitute the offence under section 308 I.P.C.
4.

In Annexure-A10 supplementary final report, the Investigating Officer has stated that there was nothing to show that the petitioner had undergone treatment in any hospital for the injuries sustained, as a result of the alleged physical assault of the second respondent.
It is further stated that the weapons used for the commission of the crime could not be recovered since it were not available at the place of occurrence.

It is pertinent to note that the incidents involved in this case are said to have happened on 22.03.2021 and 24.03.2021 at Chennai, and that further investigation was Soubhagya.M.P vs State Of Kerala on 4 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136736372/
2 conducted more than one year after the aforesaid dates.
The weapons allegedly used by the accused are a curtain rod and kitchen knife.
Therefore, the Investigating Officer cannot be found to be at fault for 2025:KER:57265 Crl.M.C No.2377/2025    5        not tracing out the weapons of offence from the crime scene.

Also, the Investigating Officer cannot be blamed for not effecting the recovery of the weapons which were in the custody of the accused, since the efforts in the above regard can only be termed as a futile exercise due to the elapse of a long period of time,
from the date of offence.

The fact that the petitioner could not bring on record anything to show that she sustained any grievous hurt due to the above assault, is also having much significance while considering the omission of the Investigating Officer in slapping the offence under section 308 I.P.C.
5.

It is true that the petitioner as well as her son had tendered statements to the effect that the second respondent had brandished a kitchen knife, placed it close to the neck of the petitioner and threatened that she would be done away with.
However, there is no case for the petitioner that the second respondent had flung the kitchen knife towards her and attempted to inflict injury.

Likewise,
the statements tendered by the petitioner and her son would not show that the alleged act of grabbing the neck of the petitioner by the second respondent was with the objective of strangulating her.

In the above 2025:KER:57265 Crl.M.C No.2377/2025    6        circumstances, it is not possible to say that the Investigating Officer went wrong in the non-inclusion of the offence under Section 308 I.P.C.
6.

Going by the definition of the offence of attempt to commit culpable homicide, envisaged under section 308 I.P.C, it is incumbent upon the prosecution to show that the accused had committed an act with such intention or knowledge that if he had caused death of the victim by the said act, he would be guilty of culpable homicide, not amounting to murder.

As far as the present case is concerned, the alleged act of the second respondent/accused hitting the petitioner with the curtain rod, grabbing her neck and placing a knife close to her neck with the threat that she would be done away with
, cannot be termed as acts which are likely to cause death.

In that view of the matter, it is not possible to say that the second respondent/accused committed the above act with such intention or knowledge that if he caused death of the petitioner by the above acts, he would be guilty of culpable homicide, not amounting to murder.

Therefore, there is absolutely no basis for the contention of the petitioner that the Investigating Officer went wrong by filing the further investigation report without including the offence under Section 308 I.P.C, and without recovering the 2025:KER:57265 Crl.M.C No.2377/2025    7        weapons of offence.
Accordingly, I find that there is absolutely no reason to interfere with Annexure-A12 order of the learned Magistrate.
In the result, the petition is hereby dismissed.

 G. GIRISH, JUDGE jsr  2025:KER:57265 Crl.M.C No.2377/2025    8
